title: Unit 7 rem early — armor as Christ; wrestling not against flesh
english: From what is written one may say that God's full armor is Christ, so "Put on the full armor of God" is the same as "Put on the Lord Jesus Christ." If the belt is truth and the breastplate righteousness, and the Savior is truth and righteousness, then the Savior is clearly the belt and the breastplate. By the same measure he himself would be the readiness of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit—which is the word of God, the living and active Word sharper than any two-edged sword.

What other full armor of God could the one who will stand against the devil's schemes even think to put on, except the virtue that is Christ? Clothed with him in all his aspects, one will be able to stand against every scheme of wickedness worked by the devil, its father. Girded with truth, he will not be pulled into assenting to persuasive, sophistic arguments for the false. Clothed with righteousness, he will stay unwounded by injustice's arrows; none of them will reach him or make the one wearing righteousness unjust.

The one who has put on the fine shoes of the gospel's readiness for peace—ready, with his works prepared for departure, and so become a person of peace—will neither do anything warlike or factious nor be condemned with the unprepared. Where the shield of faith is, unbelief hostile to the human race's salvation has no room. The one who wears the helmet of salvation keeps unbroken the head of the soul, where the divine and intelligible senses are. And as a noble soldier, holding the sword of the Spirit, which is the Lord's word, he will cut down and destroy every doctrine hostile to the truth.

"For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of the darkness, against the spiritual things of wickedness in the heavenly places" (Ephesians 6:12). Wrestling against blood and flesh, I think, means what he calls human temptations, when flesh desiring against the spirit summons us to do its works. It is no longer a human temptation, nor wrestling against blood and flesh, when Satan transforms himself into an angel of light and fights to make us attend to him as an angel of light—or anything like the things that come with every power, lying signs and wonders, and every deceit of injustice.

If the enemy persuades someone to receive him as Lord speaking in him "Thus says the Lord," so that the person even imagines himself a prophet of the God of all, he works that not as blood and flesh or a mere human temptation against one who has guarded himself this far. Therefore give the devil no place at all.

Someone will say Paul speaks this way so we will not first suppose that sins thought to come from the flesh's mindset come from flesh and blood, but from certain powers working them. There are demons that work loves and love-charms, as the prophet shows: "They were led astray by a spirit of fornication." The same may be said of demons that implant wrath and anger; even the curious summon them and are said to make an anger-binding charm. When we hate, we do not hate apart from the demons that work hatred; the so-called hate-charms support that reading.

Because the apostle wants to teach that sinning does not come to us from the body's nature, he says our wrestling is not against blood and flesh but against the rulers, the authorities, and the rest. Asking which ancient writings, revealed and shown to him, helped Paul say this, we conjecture from stories of wars and single combat—David against Goliath, Israel's sons against the foreigners or the nations they fought and conquered. title: Unit 7 rem mid — evil day; belt, breastplate, shoes, shield
english: Our wrestling, then, is against authorities that are not visible and fleshly, against world-rulers of the darkness that wraps the human race, and against spirits of wickedness that inhabit the heavenly place—that is, the air. Elsewhere he said, "in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience." The air poured around us seems filled with opposing powers.

"That you may be able to withstand in the evil day" (Ephesians 6:13). Origen: whoever seeks to withstand in the evil day must have the full armor of God the apostle set out. Through it the adversary will be shamed, with nothing base to say about us—the devil, accuser of our brothers, who also deceives sinners as his own and as belonging to his portion. Another will say the present age is an evil day. A third reading, besides those two, will say the contest does not end when someone leaves this life: even the one who has conquered here is about to fight again in another evil day against opposing energies that appear.

"Stand therefore, having girded your waist with truth" (Ephesians 6:14). Luke also writes, "Let your waists be girded." We now know what the belt is: the one who has drawn in the works of generation, no longer serves them, and hastens toward immortality girds the waist.

"And having put on the breastplate of righteousness" (Ephesians 6:14). As a breastplate makes a fighter harder to wound—especially in the vital parts—so the one clothed with righteousness will not be struck like a deer hit in the liver by an arrow, will not fall into wrath or desire, and will remain pure in heart. He wears a breastplate of righteousness forged for him by God, the craftsman of all, who prepares and gives the full armor to each of the saints.

"And having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15). Notice he named a power of the soul "feet," with which we journey, walking the one who said "I am the way." Those feet must be shod with the gospel's readiness for peace. I take the Exodus shoes required of those eating the Passover, ready for the road, as symbols of these: "Eat it with your waists girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; eat it in haste; it is the Lord's Passover." Readiness includes both hasty eating and eating while shod, so that strengthened by the food they can travel. The one still journeying must be shod; the one who has reached the holy land must untie: "Loose the shoe from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground." So the one not yet an apostle must shoe the feet with the gospel's readiness for peace; the apostle no longer takes shoes for a road—already perfected, standing and walking on holy ground, living in Christ.

"In all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one" (Ephesians 6:16). Origen: the evil one's arrows are evil thoughts. He cannot even begin to cast them into the heart when someone is covered by the shield of faith; all the flaming arrows are quenched in it. The one wearing that shield will say, "In the Lord I have trusted; how will you say to my soul, Flee to the mountains like a sparrow? For look, sinners have stretched a bow and prepared arrows for a quiver, to shoot the upright in heart in a moonless place." Since I have trusted in the Lord, how do you advise me not to stand against the bows and quivered arrows sinners aim, wanting to wound the upright in heart? Look: I have stood; I do not flee; and all the flaming arrows of the evil one will be quenched almost at once.

title: Unit 7 rem close — Spirit's sword; bold speech; peace and incorruption
english: —petition for all the saints and for me. The healthy word flows from a divine spirit; the opposing word speaks from the earth. The one who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks from the earth; the one who comes from heaven is above all, and what he has seen and heard he witnesses. The word from the Spirit is a sword; that is why Paul here calls the sword of the Spirit the word of God. For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword; it penetrates as far as the division of soul and spirit, cuts and divides, and also works through prayer and petition for those who pray at every time and pray in the Spirit, according to "I will pray with the spirit." It works for those who watch in order to grow rich in God's word and persist in gaining it, so they may help others and, through prayers, work with those who help. Notice also the apostle's moderation: he asks the Ephesians for petitions on his behalf.

"That speech may be given me in the opening of my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel" (Ephesians 6:19). Origen: when the mouth is opened after speech has been given, the mystery of the gospel is made known with boldness, no longer in proverbs and parables. The Savior says the same: "An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but will announce the Father to you with boldness." Only the person whose heart does not condemn can hold a word spoken with boldness—and every such person can—because if the heart does not condemn, we have boldness toward God, and whatever we ask we receive from him. So the one who makes the mystery known with boldness is rare, because rare is the one who has boldness toward God. Who will boast of a pure heart? Who will speak boldly of being clean from sins?

"But that you also may know my affairs, what I am doing, Tychicus the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord will make everything known to you, whom I sent to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us and that he may encourage your hearts" (Ephesians 6:21–22). Because the apostle's whole life, every act and energy, happened by the Word of God with Christ living in him, he sends Tychicus to announce to the Ephesians the rule of his life and the order of his deeds. It was fitting that, so the Ephesians might have a pattern of good conduct, he send Tychicus for that very reason. They would also be encouraged as they learned that the best things, and those fitting an apostle, were being accomplished in Paul.

"Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" (Ephesians 6:23). Origen: if any other gift is given from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, peace is one too—among the most honored gifts, the peace that surpasses every mind, which will guard the hearts and thoughts of the saints. It is a calm and fair weather of the soul, foreign to every storm, unrest, and passion. Likewise love with faith is a gift from God and the Lord Jesus Christ: love toward God with the whole heart and what follows, and toward the neighbor as oneself. The one who has received love as a gift also shows it toward enemies, hating no one and praying for those who abuse him.

"Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption" (Ephesians 6:24). Some have explained loving him in incorruption as being pure from the works of corruption, and they take those works as sexual intercourse—hence custom calls the pure from intercourse "incorrupt" and those who have tasted mixing "corrupted." Others stretch "If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him" that way, and then cannot save "But each has his own gift from God, one this way, another that." See whether every sin can be corruption of the soul, and complete abstinence from it incorruption. Then those who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption are those who abstain from every sin; and with all of them is the grace of God. Since there are some who love the Lord yet do not love him in incorruption, Paul says, "Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption."
